summary: Today’s pulse tracks Two bodies found after avalanche hits Himalayan climbing group, UK politics live: Pat McFadden tells Labour activists they should not defend benefits system ‘status quo’ because it ‘writes off’ claimants, and Woman charged with stealing from patients and staff at hospitals across Ontario. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are labour, system, and people. In the background, Changing UK benefits for young people a ‘moral crusade’, says minister and UN ambassador Waltz says Iran was not negotiating ‘in good faith’ to end war keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Two bodies found after avalanche hits Himalayan climbing group
headlines.description: Rescuers are looking for at least 10 Nepalese people who were preparing to take climbers up the Himlung Himal peak.

headlines.title: UK politics live: Pat McFadden tells Labour activists they should not defend benefits system ‘status quo’ because it ‘writes off’ claimants
headlines.description: Work and pensions secretary says the current system is flawed because it consigns too many people to a life on benefits when they would be better off working ‘I can deliver’: Burnham pledges radical change on eve of Labour conference Kuenssberg puts it to Burnham that, according to the Health Foundation, a system offering adult social care free at the point of delivery (like healthcare delivered by the NHS) would cost £18bn. Burnham says the cost is “not that high” (ie, not as high as £18bn). Not that high. But can I directly deal with this issue of the costs? Louise Casey is still doing an official review for us, so I will set out the vision, if you like, on Tuesday [in his speech to the conference]. Louise will then help us with the how. How do we make this happen? When can we make it happen?

headlines.title: Woman charged with stealing from patients and staff at hospitals across Ontario
headlines.description: The 34-year-old is under investigation for incidents that began in February 2024 up until as recently as last month.

headlines.title: Changing UK benefits for young people a ‘moral crusade’, says minister
headlines.description: Pat McFadden urges Labour MPs to back overhauls, amid signs party looking to cut payments for some 16- to 24-year-olds UK politics live – latest updates Labour MPs have a moral responsibility to accept significant changes to the welfare system to help get more young people into work, the work and pensions secretary has said. In a sign he is looking to overhaul the welfare state, Pat McFadden said it was time for Labour to “renew” the system first created by the Clement Attlee government and given a new deal by New Labour.

headlines.title: UN ambassador Waltz says Iran was not negotiating ‘in good faith’ to end war
headlines.description: Waltz says Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to end war because they ‘were asking for everything up front’ The Trump administration ’s ambassador to the United Nations said the US rejected Iran ’s proposal to end the ongoing war there because Iranian negotiators “were asking for everything up front”. Echoing comments by Donald Trump on Saturday, the president’s UN ambassador Mike Waltz told CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday that Iran had asked for relief “from billions and billions of sanctions that are going into place” as part of an economic blockade on Iran. The blockade is aimed at putting pressure on Iran to stop its attacks ‌on vessels in the strait of Hormuz.

headlines.title: Most of UK’s essential food supply grown in drought-risk areas, report warns
headlines.description: Keys crops such as cereals, potatoes, sugar and oils grown in areas with moderate to very high risk The vast majority of the UK’s essential foods, including cereals, potatoes, sugar and oil, are grown in areas of England rated as having a moderate to very high risk of drought. A very high proportion – 81% – of England’s fresh produce is concentrated in parts of the country that are already experiencing water stress, according to the analysis by the nature-focused investment fund Rebalance Earth .

headlinePool.title: Nor’easter storm batters US east coast with heavy winds and power outages
headlinePool.description: At least one person killed and nearly 150,000 households lost electricity from North Carolina to New England A strong, deadly storm known as a nor’easter battered the US’s east coast over the weekend, bringing power outages, flooding, damaging winds and hazardous ocean conditions. Trees and power lines were knocked down across the region, at least one person was killed and hundreds of thousands were left without electricity as officials cautioned that conditions could deteriorate further.

headlinePool.title: Venezuela releases dozens of political prisoners as election calls grow
headlinePool.description: A slew of dissidents being released from long-term detention comes days after the nation's interim leader met the US president.

headlinePool.title: Burnham dodges questions on Heathrow third runway as project faces four-year delay
headlinePool.description: Airport chiefs say 2035 operations deadline unachievable as critics say new delay makes case for project ‘even more dubious’ Plans for a third runway at Heathrow are once again up in the air after the prime minister refused to say whether he backs the “contested” project which is delayed by up to four years. Over the weekend it emerged that ​Heathrow no longer expects to meet the original 2035 deadline. Instead, the airport hopes to secure planning permission by 2029 and then open the runway “within a decade”, meaning it would not be operational until 2039.

headlinePool.title: Tense standoff over loyalist march in Portadown as protesters block route
headlinePool.description: Sinn Féin leaders join those on streets opposing decision to allow Garvaghy Road parade for first time since 1998 Portadown march: latest updates Hundreds of protesters spent the day blocking the route of a hugely contentious parade in Northern Ireland after a court gave late-night clearance for the Orange Order to march on a historically significant road for the first time in nearly 30 years. The loyalist Drumcree parade along the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown was given the go-ahead by the Parades Commission for the first time since 1998, a decision denounced by Sinn Féin as “madness”.

headlinePool.title: Pope Leo urges healing of ‘deep wounds’ before meeting child sexual abuse survivors in France
headlinePool.description: Pontiff also uses visit to Catholic shrine at Lourdes to criticise assisted dying as ‘false compassion’ The pope has called on the Catholic church to heal “deep wounds” and “painful errors”, before a meeting with survivors of child sexual abuse as he continues his four-day visit to France. Addressing a crowd in a large field near the Catholic shrine of Lourdes on Sunday, Pope Leo XIV called on the church to reckon with its past, without directly referencing sexual abuse scandals in France that affected at least 330,000 children over seven decades.

headlinePool.title: Swiss voters reject stricter neutrality rules that would have curbed Nato cooperation
headlinePool.description: 70% vote against tightening centuries-old neutrality, which far right said was being eroded by sanctions against Russia Swiss voters have decisively rejected a proposal for a strict definition of neutrality that would have required Switzerland to curb cooperation with Nato and abandon sanctions against Russia. All cantons and about 70% of voters rejected the proposal for a strictly defined version of neutrality to be ⁠written into the Swiss constitution, final results from the Federal Statistical Office showed. The motion had been promoted by the far-right Swiss People’s party (SVP).

headlinePool.title: One Nation boss called David Farley an ‘asshole’ in lead-up to Farrer byelection, text messages reveal
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: Documents seen by Guardian Australia show that Kelvin Morton has also clashed with party HQ staff and Brisbane volunteers In a series of text messages seen by Guardian Australia, Morton responds to a news article published in the Sydney Morning Herald about infighting among senior party figures over Farley’s previously undeclared support for the Labor party. headlinePool.title: British celebrities beat AI companies lobbying to get free use of their work. They have a warning for Australia
headlinePool.description: ‘People care about the songs, books and pictures that influence the critical moments in their lives,’ says the architect of the fightback in the UK If there is one lesson to be learned from a similar battle in the UK, high-profile members of the creative industries make a difference. They get your argument on the front of newspapers, in the news bulletins and on social media.
